contents.name: Corollary 25.13
contents.reason: This classifies all irreducible highest-weight modules, whereas this page only constructs the quotient L(lambda). The general classification belongs to the established highest-weight interface and later linkage development, not to the form-and-determinant proof.

sources.title: Mrudul Thatte, Category O: Verma's Thesis
sources.locator: Read the complete six-page PDF: Sections 1–6, printed/PDF pp. 1–6, from `1 Contravariant Forms` through the end of `6 Error in Verma's Thesis`. Sections 1–5 are the independent full treatment; Section 6 is read and explicitly rejected because the source marks its claimed results false.

fetch_verified.note: Opened as the full PDF and read at the stated range; the page count and source URL were verified directly.

contents.name: Proposition 1.2(c)
contents.reason: The tensor-product form is a separate construction on two modules. No tensor-product representation construction is needed to define, normalize, or use the form on one Verma module in this pair.

contents.name: Proposition 1.2(d)
contents.reason: The orthogonal-complement submodule statement is a general form tool. The planned radical proof uses contravariance and the unique maximal Verma submodule, so no complement formalism is required here.

contents.name: Proposition 1.2(e)
contents.reason: Orthogonality of distinct central-character summands belongs to block decomposition in Category O. This pair constructs one Verma form and does not introduce the ambient category or its central-character summands.

contents.name: 2, Simple Submodules of Verma Modules
contents.reason: This develops the distinct question of a unique simple submodule. The selected construction needs the unique simple quotient; relating the two requires the later Verma-homomorphism or duality machinery.

contents.name: Proposition 2.1
contents.reason: Its unique-simple-submodule statement is not used by the maximal-submodule quotient argument. It belongs with the later study of embeddings and duality rather than being an omitted prerequisite here.

contents.name: 3, Homomorphisms between Verma Modules
contents.reason: This is precisely the next representation-theory pair's subject: it turns singular vectors into maps and studies their dimensions. The present page supplies the universal property it will consume without pre-empting that development.

contents.name: Theorem 3.1
contents.reason: The injectivity and dimension bound for maps between Verma modules are RL-3 statements. They are not needed for constructing a Verma module, its form, or the determinant criterion on this page.

contents.name: Remark 3.2
contents.reason: The convention that identifies a nonzero Verma homomorphism with an embedding belongs to the next page's map-and-linkage discussion. It is not needed to form the present quotient or compute its determinant blocks.

contents.name: Theorem 4.2
contents.reason: The theorem's embedding conclusion is an instance of the Verma embedding criterion. That criterion is deliberately scheduled in RL-3 after this page has established singular vectors and determinant hyperplanes.

contents.name: Corollary 4.4
contents.reason: This identifies a simple submodule along a dot orbit and uses the embedding story deferred to RL-3. The current page's rank-one quotient example does not require this general linkage consequence.

contents.name: 5, Block Decomposition of Category O
contents.reason: Block decomposition requires the ambient Category O, finite length, and central-character organization. Those definitions and finiteness obligations belong to the explicitly scheduled RL-4 page.

contents.name: Theorem 5.1
contents.reason: Identifying linked subcategories as the blocks is a Category O theorem. It depends on the category and its composition-factor framework, both intentionally deferred to the dedicated RL-4 page.

contents.name: 6, Error in Verma's Thesis
contents.reason: The source itself marks this section false. It is retained in the harvest as a warning, not weakened into a new library claim or used as support for a theorem.

contents.name: Lemma 6.1
contents.reason: The source explicitly says that its proof has a gap. A scaffold may not turn a documented false claim into a library lemma merely because it is relevant to submodule generation.

contents.name: Theorem 6.2
contents.reason: This claimed generation of every submodule by maximal vectors rests on the preceding false lemma. It is deliberately excluded rather than being silently repaired or used in the singular-vector argument.

contents.name: 8, Highest weight modules and Verma modules
Corollary 8.10
contents.reason: The classification of irreducible highest-weight modules is broader than the quotient construction selected here. It is a consequence after the present construction, not a lemma required by the form or determinant proof.

contents.name: Proposition 8.12
contents.reason: This is the finite-dimensional classification criterion for arbitrary semisimple g. The page supplies one explicit sl2 quotient as a boundary check, but does not undertake the dominant-integral classification theorem.

contents.name: Exercise 8.13
contents.reason: This exercise introduces expectation values and contragredient Verma modules. Those dual and tensor constructions are neither required for the single-Verma Shapovalov form nor within this pair's stated scope.

contents.name: Exercise 8.14
contents.reason: These exercises construct homomorphisms and embeddings between Verma modules. They are the intended subject of RL-3 and are not assumed by the determinant proof on the current page.

contents.name: Definition 15.1
contents.reason: The categorical finiteness definition is expressly scheduled for RL-4. Only the formal-character calculation is needed now, and it is stated with its completed-series convention rather than importing Category O.

contents.name: Example 15.2
contents.reason: The example places Verma and contragredient Verma modules inside Category O. The former is constructed here, while the Category O and restricted-dual assertions belong to the later finiteness-and-duality page.

contents.name: Lemma 15.3
contents.reason: This lemma supplies Category O finiteness beyond one Verma module. The present page proves directly that each PBW weight space is finite and leaves category-wide structure to RL-4.
